source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Forming a protective barrier over the ulcer, rather than reducing acid production or neutralizing acid directly as the client is currently assuming","B":"Directly neutralizing stomach acid, identical to an antacid, similar to what the client is currently assuming about how this medication works","C":"Working systemically rather than at the local ulcer site, which does not describe how this particular medication actually works","D":"Working through the same acid-reducing mechanism as a PPI, which does not describe how this particular medication actually works"}}
source_row.rationale: Sucralfate works by forming a protective, adhesive barrier or coating over an ulcer site (particularly effective in an acidic environment), shielding the damaged mucosa from further injury by stomach acid and pepsin, a distinct mechanism from antacids (which neutralize acid) or PPIs/H2 blockers (which reduce acid production).
source_row.source_detail: Mechanism of Action as a Mucosal Protectant
